what_its_for: Interferon beta-1a is used to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS). It helps reduce the number of MS flare-ups (relapses) and slows down the worsening of disability. It does not cure MS, but it can help manage the disease and improve your quality of life.
how_to_take: This medicine is given as an injection. Avonex is injected into a muscle (intramuscular), usually in the thigh or upper arm, once a week. Rebif is injected under the skin (subcutaneous), usually in the thigh, stomach area, or upper arm, three times a week. Your doctor or nurse will teach you how to give yourself the injection properly. Always rotate injection sites to prevent skin irritation. Use a new needle and syringe or auto-injector pen each time. Never share your injection device with anyone else.
dosing: Avonex: The usual dose is 30 micrograms (mcg) injected into a muscle once every week, on the same day each week. Rebif: The usual starting dose is 8.8 mcg or 22 mcg injected under the skin three times per week, gradually increasing over 4 weeks to the full dose of 22 mcg or 44 mcg three times per week. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose of Avonex, take it as soon as you remember, then wait at least 7 days before your next dose. If you miss a dose of Rebif, take it as soon as possible, but skip it if your next scheduled dose is in less than 2 days. Do not take two doses on the same day. Never double up to make up for a missed dose. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store this medication in the refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Do not freeze it. If needed, Avonex prefilled syringes or autoinjector pens can be kept at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C) for up to 7 days. Keep it away from direct light and heat. Do not use the medication if it looks cloudy, discolored, or has particles in it. Dispose of used needles and syringes safely in a puncture-resistant sharps container.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol or limit it, as alcohol may worsen side effects like liver problems. Do not take other medications, including over-the-counter drugs and herbal supplements, without checking with your doctor first. Avoid getting live vaccines while on this medication without talking to your doctor. Try to avoid overheating (hot baths, saunas), as heat can temporarily worsen MS symptoms. Use sunscreen and protective clothing, as this medicine may make your skin more sensitive to the sun.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you have: signs of a serious allergic reaction (trouble breathing, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, severe rash); severe depression, thoughts of suicide, or unusual mood changes; signs of liver problems (yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, severe stomach pain, unusual tiredness); signs of infection (fever over 100.4°F, chills, cough, painful urination); severe pain, redness, or a lump at the injection site; seizures; chest pain or trouble breathing; or any new or worsening symptoms of MS. Also tell your doctor if you have flu-like symptoms that are very severe or do not improve with over-the-counter pain relievers.
when_it_works: Interferon beta-1a starts working in your body right away, but you may not notice changes immediately. It may take several months to a year or more before you see a clear reduction in MS relapses. It is important to keep taking this medication as prescribed even if you feel well, because it is working to prevent future flare-ups in the background.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of this medication during pregnancy is not fully known. Use effective birth control while taking this medicine. It is not known if it passes into breast milk, so discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. Elderly patients: This medication has not been extensively studied in people over 65 years old. Use with caution and follow your doctor's guidance. Children: This medication is generally not recommended for children under 18 years of age. Kidney or liver problems: If you have liver disease or elevated liver enzymes, tell your doctor before starting this medication, as it can affect the liver. Regular blood tests will be needed to monitor your liver function.
